pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words, with at least one answer grounded in their own NOTES.md numbers; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: Walk me through the four packages of taskd and which way the dependencies point. Then: to move storage from SQLite to Postgres, what do you change?
expected_points: cmd/taskd wires everything; httpapi is the HTTP edge; task is the domain; sqlitestore is storage
httpapi and sqlitestore both import task; task imports neither, so the domain depends on nobody
task.Store is declared by the consumer, so a new package satisfying it plus one line in main is the whole change
migrations live with the storage implementation and are append-only
handlers stay thin: decode, delegate, encode

questions.prompt: Explain the token strategy you shipped: how a request proves who it is, why the comparison is written the way it is, and three things this scheme does NOT protect against.
expected_points: Authorization: Bearer <token> against tokens configured in the environment, never a default in source
digests compared with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare so response timing leaks neither the token nor its length
a bearer token is a shared secret: no expiry, no scopes, revocation means editing config and restarting
plaintext HTTP exposes it to every proxy, so TLS is required; tokens go in headers, never in URLs
anyone who can read the logs must not find it there — hence nothing but method/path/status/duration/request_id

questions.prompt: Your API is 'failing'. Using only what taskd exposes, what do you look at and in what order — and what does /healthz tell you that /readyz doesn't?
expected_points: metrics answer 'is it broken and how badly': http_requests_total by status, duration histogram, in-flight
the access log answers 'which requests and where', and request_id follows one request across its lines
healthz is liveness and touches nothing; readyz pings the database and reports 503 when storage is unusable
a liveness probe that checks dependencies gets healthy processes killed during someone else's outage
traces are the missing pillar; request_id is a poor substitute that stops at the process boundary

questions.prompt: Describe the levels of your test suite. What does the httptest suite catch that the service-layer tests cannot, and vice versa?
expected_points: service tests are unit-level over a fake store, with no httptest and a fake clock — they check rules, fast
the httptest suite drives the real router over a real SQLite database: routing, status codes, envelopes, auth, wiring
store tests are integration-level, each on its own temp-file database so tests stay isolated
the API suite catches wiring and mapping mistakes; unit tests point at the broken rule instead of a status code
everything runs under -race because handlers share the service and the store across goroutines

questions.prompt: Where does an error become a status code, and what reaches the client versus the log? Then tell me the one performance decision you measured, with numbers.
expected_points: one function (respondError) maps validation/not-found/conflict/bad-request/default onto 400/404/409/400/500
adding a domain error later is one new case there, not a hunt through handlers
the client gets a generic 'internal error'; the log gets the real error plus request_id
the measured decision is the tasks(status) index: benchmark numbers with and without it, on fresh databases
names the index's cost (write amplification, space) and what would justify dropping it

questions.prompt: A deploy sends SIGTERM while requests are in flight. Trace what happens, and explain why requestTimeout < WriteTimeout < shutdownGrace.
expected_points: signal.NotifyContext cancels the run context; Run calls srv.Shutdown with a grace deadline
Shutdown stops accepting, closes idle connections, and waits for active handlers; Serve returns ErrServerClosed, which is success
the grace period must exceed the request budget or shutdown cuts off requests that were still allowed to run
TimeoutHandler answers the client with 503 but cannot kill the handler goroutine — it stops when it checks its context

questions.prompt: Justify the middleware order — and tell me what breaks if AccessLog and Recover swap places, or if Auth wrapped the whole mux.
expected_points: RequestID outermost so every inner log line and the response header carry the same id
AccessLog outside Recover so a panic still yields one access line with status 500
Timeout innermost so it bounds the handler, not the middleware
Auth inside Routes so probes and scrapes need no credentials
the trade-off: the access log cannot name the client because Auth runs deeper than it
